title: Anisotropic Ion Migration and Electronic Conduction in van der Waals Ferroelectric CuInP2S6

nodes.label: vdW electronic devices need controlled ionic manipulation in layered ferroelectric/dielectric materials

requires_unseen: closing sentence linked to F1; introduction not in packet

nodes.label: Whether Cu ion migration in CIPS follows distinct in-plane and out-of-plane paths is not directly resolved at the nanoscale
Use a cleaved CuInP2S6 flake that has chemically separated into ferroelectric CIPS and paraelectric IPS regions

requires_unseen: Cu deficiency separates the crystal into In4/3P2S6 (IPS) and CuInP2S6 (CIPS)

nodes.label: Probe the same flake region with colocated PFM and c-AFM, the biased tip acting as local field source and current probe

requires_unseen: that the PFM and c-AFM images are of the same region is stated in the F4 caption
that the biased tip acts as both field source and current probe is stated in the linked text

nodes.label: Vary tip scan speed (2, 0.5 um/s), ramp speed (0.5, 1, 2 V/s), tip bias (0 to -8 V) and bias-off time (1, 30, 60 s)

attrs.variable: field exposure time per unit area
requires_unseen: scan speeds 2 and 0.5 um/s and ramp speeds 0.5, 1 and 2 V/s, from the F4 caption
the 0 V -> -8 V -> +8 V ramp and the 30/1/60 s bias-off durations, from the F4 and F6 captions and linked text

nodes.label: Cleave the CIPS crystal and transfer the flake onto a PMMA/PEN substrate sputtered with a gold bottom electrode

requires_unseen: cleaving, flake transfer and gold sputtering are stated in the F3c caption; the schematic shows only the finished stack

nodes.label: Hold a DC tip bias of -3 to -8 V on the CIPS phase for 60-300 s, in air and in N2

requires_unseen: the 300 s holding time is stated only in the F5 linked text
the -8 V bias-on cycle of 60 s is stated in the F6 caption
F5 itself is labelled only 0, -4, -5 and -6 V; the -3.0 V hold is annotated on F4b

nodes.label: The flake surface is a network of ferroelectric CIPS lamellae embedded in a paraelectric IPS matrix

requires_unseen: CIPS = ferroelectric CuInP2S6
IPS = paraelectric In4/3P2S6

nodes.label: The CIPS phase conducts under a -3 V tip bias while the surrounding IPS phase stays insulating
CIPS conductivity rises with how long the material is held in the tip field (slower scan, slower ramp, longer hold)
The tip field drags mobile Cu+ toward the biased contact, raising the local mobile-carrier density and the current
Poling leaves a Cu-rich zone in the biased CIPS region
Long-range Cu migration away from equilibrium positions collapses the biased area into a surface depression

attrs.depth_text: linked text states a subsided structure of about -2.5 nm

nodes.label: Conduction in the CIPS phase is dominantly ionic, carried by Cu+ migration, not purely electronic
Two Cu+ paths operate: fast in-plane intralayer hopping (stage I) and slower out-of-plane interlayer hopping across the vdW gap (stage II)

requires_unseen: the assignment of stage I to the in-plane path and stage II to the out-of-plane path is argued from the activation energies in the F6 linked text; no panel shows it
attrs.image_note: F6h and the F6g insets are the authors' proposed model drawing, not data

nodes.label: Nanoscale ionic conduction of the CIPS flake on a flexible PMMA/PEN substrate is switched and amplified electrically at room temperature

attrs.condition: room temperature, air and N2, DC tip bias

nodes.label: Cu ion migration and the resulting conduction in vdW ferroelectric CIPS are anisotropic, with the easier in-plane path, guiding vdW ionic-electronic device design

requires_unseen: the paper's closing device-design statement

nodes.label: Out-of-plane PFM phase map splits the field into a uniform region labelled 1 IPS and isolated patches labelled 2 CIPS with opposite (180 deg) phase
Piezoresponse amplitude along the marked line alternates between about 5 pm/V on IPS segments and 15-24 pm/V on three CIPS segments over 0.85 um
Topography of the same area is smooth within the -5 to 7 nm scale and carries no counterpart of the PFM phase pattern

attrs.image_note: rules out a topographic origin of the piezoresponse contrast

nodes.label: The c-AFM map at -3.0 V shows a conducting network down to -1.6 pA that coincides with the high-amplitude PFM network of the same region; the surround carries about 0 pA
Current profiles across the same box reach -1.6 pA at 2 um/s and about -110 pA at 0.5 um/s, a roughly 70-fold increase at the slower scan

attrs.image_note: linked text states about 60-fold; the plotted minima give about 70-fold

nodes.label: On CIPS the current turns on below about -4 V and reaches -5.5 pA at -8 V, while on IPS it stays near 0 pA over the whole +/-8 V sweep

attrs.image_note: the inset cycles at 0.5, 1 and 2 V/s rank the same way, about -450 pA at 0.5 V/s vs about -200 pA at 2 V/s, but are too small to read precisely

nodes.label: At a fixed -4 V the CIPS current grows steadily from 0 to about -700 pA over 300 s while the IPS current stays at 0
Topography slices become progressively more depressed along the CIPS network as the tip bias is stepped 0, -4, -5, -6 V

attrs.image_note: the c-AFM colour-bar minima widen over the same series, -1.3 -> -6.0 -> -6.5 pA in air

nodes.label: The topographic and c-AFM changes with bias are the same in air and in N2
After poling at -6 V the topography of the poled area shows a dark, subsided band network
The SEM-EDS Cu map of the poled area shows Cu-rich bands tracing the same network as the pre-poling PFM amplitude image

attrs.image_note: the Cu map is speckle-noisy; the enrichment reads as denser cyan along the bands, not as a sharp contrast

nodes.label: The first bias-on maximum current is comparable in the three runs: -11, -14 and -17 pA
With -8 V on / 30 s off cycling the current falls to zero at every bias-off and recovers as soon as the bias returns
The bias-on current restarts higher at each successive cycle, reaching about -230 pA by 800 s
In the 230-330 s window the bias-on current falls in two segments: a steep drop to about -12 pA labelled Stage I, then a shallower linear fall to -50 pA labelled Stage II
With a 1 s bias-off the steep initial segment is absent and the current falls in one slope, unlike the 30 s bias-off run

attrs.image_note: at the printed scale the first seconds of each cycle are only a few pixels; the single-slope reading is weaker than the two-stage reading in F6g

nodes.label: The PFM phase map marks only a few small CIPS patches while the amplitude map of the same area shows an extensive CIPS network
Alternative: electrochemical formation of metal oxides under the biased tip could produce the surface change

requires_unseen: the linked text names metal-oxide formation as the interference being excluded

nodes.label: CIPS is electron-beam sensitive and cracks formed on the surface during the EDS mapping

requires_unseen: cracks reported for Figure S7a, which is not in the packet

nodes.label: In CIPS the Cu+ occupies three sites: Cu1 quasi-trigonal with up/down states, Cu2 octahedral, and Cu3 almost tetrahedral, penetrating the vdW gap

requires_unseen: the site geometries (quasi-trigonal, octahedral, almost tetrahedral, penetrating the vdW gap) are named only in the linked text; F3b labels only Cu1, Cu2, Cu3 and the up/down sites

nodes.label: Reported activation energies are higher out-of-plane than in-plane: Ea = 0.85/0.23 eV and EA = 1.16/0.55 eV (OOP/IP), with EA = Ea + Ec

requires_unseen: activation-energy values and the EA = Ea + Ec relation cited from refs 6, 24, 25

nodes.label: Conductivity that grows with slower scanning or more cycles is a known activation signature of ionic conductors such as KTiOPO4

requires_unseen: KTiOPO4 precedent cited in the linked text

nodes.label: CIPS has Tc = 310 K and its ionic conductivity onsets near 250 K, so Cu hopping is thermally activated at room temperature

requires_unseen: Tc = 310 K and the 250 K onset cited from refs 6, 34

notes: Packet figure ids are offset from the paper's own numbering: F1 is the TOC graphic, F2 is a journal-cover thumbnail with no scientific content, and F3-F6 are the paper's Figures 1-4. Both F1 and F2 carry an empty caption. The panel detector tags F3g (a PFM phase line profile) with cue class 'XRD', evidently from the '(deg' axis token; the equivalent amplitude line profile F3h has no cue class and was cited instead, so no AFM node is hung on an XRD-cued panel. Information lost: the supplementary figures S1-S11 carry the four-point bias/holding-time series, the +6 V non-conducting c-AFM control, the repeated I-V cycling and the full element maps; none are in the packet, so the graph rests on F3-F6 only. The argument branches at the biased CIPS region into a conduction branch (n9, n10, n14) and a structural branch (n12, n13), which rejoin at n15. Judge: o14 was split (bias-off reset vs cycle-to-cycle growth); the ruled-out oxide route a1 now contrasts with n13 instead of being a second cause, so n13 has one cause and needs no mode.

a1 -> n13 changed from causes (mode alternative) to contrasts: the metal-oxide route is ruled out, so calling it a co-cause would be wrong and no caption or figure poses the choice; the exclusion is already carried by o10 -rules_out-> a1
